source_text: Let's just retire codex-18 and codex-19 since we're not pursuing LISP work now anyway.  You can delete them.

fragments.text: Let's just retire codex-18 and codex-19 since we're not pursuing LISP work now anyway.

reply_text:
㊥ (codex-18 and codex-19 retired) Done. I cancelled codex-18's running job, stopped codex-19's background regression run, and deregistered both agents. `GET /api/alpha/agents` no longer lists either. Their committed work stays on its branches. The four rows they had are now unassigned in the status report, with notes on where to resume.

㊢ (what was in flight, and where it stands)
- **codex-18, `psw-proj9`.** The per-application metavariable fix was cancelled before any fix commit. The branch `psw/ascription-fold` is at b99a088e. It has cand-1 merged in and the hygienic-name fix 5863a7fd with its tests. The cause, written up in proj8's report, and the saved lambda patch are enough to resume from.
- **codex-19, `atEnd`.** The branch `psw/prop-bool-coercion` is at 3e37a458, with explicit-argument instantiation, unify-before-coerce and the unnamed-slot fix. Its real-importer regression was stopped before a result, so that fix is untested on the production path.
- **Uncommitted edits.** Neither worktree had any.

㊩ (a slip) While stopping codex-19's run, I used a process match that also hit my own tool shell and killed it. Nothing else was affected: the regression run shows as exited, and no probe processes remain in those worktrees.

㊢ (records updated)
- `rowstatus.json`: `atEnd`, `mkEOIError`, `FileMap.ofString` with its loop, and `Array.back!` now show in the backlog.
- The queue file has a "Retired" section with each branch and resume note.
- Memory: the Lisp-port and seat-reservation entries now say both seats are retired.

🈳 (seats now) Three sol seats remain:
- codex-4: `psw-sigma14`, then instance naming;
- codex-17: `psw-default10`;
- codex-6: checking the 11 untested rows.

The four orphaned rows wait for whichever seat frees first. The per-application metavariable fix comes first, since it's shared and may move several rows.

previous_reply_acts.text: (work in progress) Agreed: READY and WAITING describe rows nobody is working on, so they don't belong there. WORK IN PROGRESS now shows, for each row being worked on, who is on it and what they're doing. If the row also depends on a failing row that nobody has taken, it adds a "will also need" line. The READY, NEEDS A CHECK and BLOCKED sections now list only unassigned rows, so the two groups no longer overlap.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (what "will also need" shows) Even when codex-4 clears `β`, `mkDeclExt` won't compile until four other failing rows do, and nobody is on those yet. Two of them are the instance-naming rows at the top of the ready list. So repairing instance naming would also unblock `mkDeclExt`.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (where the status comes from) The "doing" text lives in `rowstatus.json`. I update it each time I dispatch or close a job, so it's only as current as my last dispatch.
